whyThisMatters: Naming the trick helps you spot it. If the group cannot say "urgency trap" or "domain spoofing" out loud together, you will not catch it under pressure on your own.
rememberThis: If you can name the trick, you can spot it next time. Put a word to what felt strange.

discussionPrompts: Ask someone to define one of these terms in their own words before you show the answer. Could they explain it to a coworker who missed today?
Ask which two terms are easiest to mix up and why. Fake link and fake portal are the most confused.
Ask for a real example from their own inbox or phone that matches one of these terms.
facilitatorNotes.commonWrongAnswer: People most often mix up FAKE LINK and FAKE PORTAL. Both involve a wrong destination. So people pick one when the riddle points to the other.

riddles.riddle: I am a fake HR email. You see hr@synergymarine-group-careers.com. But the real one is hr@synergymarinegroup.com. I just added one extra word. What am I?
I say "ACT NOW or you will lose your pay!" and "Do not call your boss, just click here!" I want you to hurry and not think. What am I?
You think I am a PDF payslip. But my name ends with .pdf.exe. I also say "Enable Content" to open me. What am I?
You see portal.synergymarinegroup.com in blue. But when you hover, I go to a site with "-secure" in the name. What am I?
I look just like the real crew login page. But my address has one extra letter "n" - synergymanne. What am I?
I am a fake text message on your phone. I ask you to tap a short link about a package or an urgent account problem. What am I?
A box pops up and says "Type your password here to fix the error." Real IT never does this in a pop-up. What am I?
I send you many "Approve?" messages again and again. I want to make you tired so you tap Approve by mistake. What am I?
Remember 3 steps: 1. Stop, 2. Verify on a known number, 3. Report to IT. What is this rule called?
